title: Body & Health (身体与健康)
description: Name body parts, describe symptoms like a cold, a fever or a headache, talk to a doctor, say what you should do with 应该, and discuss healthy habits such as exercise, rest and drinking water.

notes.heading: 💪 Body Parts (身体 shēntǐ)
notes.body:
身体 **shēntǐ** means 'body'. Key parts:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 头 | tóu | head |
| 眼睛 | yǎnjing | eye(s) |
| 耳朵 | ěrduo | ear(s) |
| 鼻子 | bízi | nose |
| 嘴 | zuǐ | mouth |
| 手 | shǒu | hand |
| 脚 | jiǎo | foot / feet |
| 腿 | tuǐ | leg |
| 肚子 | dùzi | stomach / tummy |

💡 **Worked Example:** 他用眼睛看，用耳朵听。Tā yòng yǎnjing kàn, yòng ěrduo tīng. — He uses his eyes to see and his ears to hear. (用 **yòng** = to use)

📎 **Key Points:**
- 睛 in 眼睛 and 朵 in 耳朵 are neutral-tone second syllables.
- Count body parts: 两只手 (two hands), 一双眼睛 (a pair of eyes).

notes.heading: 🤒 Sickness & Symptoms
notes.body:
| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 生病 | shēngbìng | to get sick |
| 感冒 | gǎnmào | (to have) a cold |
| 发烧 | fāshāo | (to have) a fever |
| 头疼 | tóuténg | headache |
| 肚子疼 | dùzi téng | stomach ache |
| 咳嗽 | késou | (to) cough |
| 不舒服 | bù shūfu | unwell / not comfortable |

💡 **Worked Example:** 我感冒了，还咳嗽。Wǒ gǎnmào le, hái késou. — I've caught a cold, and I'm coughing too. (还 **hái** = also/still)

📎 **Key Points:**
- 生病 shēngbìng is literally 'produce illness' — a verb phrase: 他生病了 (he got sick).
- 不舒服 bù shūfu is a gentle, all-purpose way to say you feel unwell.
- 了 **le** after the verb marks that the change has happened: 我感冒了 = I've caught a cold.

notes.heading: 😣 Saying What Hurts: 疼 and 痛
notes.body:
**Pattern:** body part + 疼/痛 = that part hurts.

- **疼 téng** — the everyday spoken word for 'ache/hurt'
- **痛 tòng** — also 'pain', common in compounds like 头痛 (headache, more formal)

💡 **Worked Example:**
- 我头疼。Wǒ tóu téng. — I have a headache. (literally: my head hurts)
- 我肚子疼。Wǒ dùzi téng. — My tummy hurts.
- 我的腿很痛。Wǒ de tuǐ hěn tòng. — My leg really hurts.

🔑 **How it works:** no verb 'to have' is needed — the body part is the subject and 疼 is what it does. To ask someone: 你哪儿疼？Nǐ nǎr téng? — Where does it hurt? (哪儿 **nǎr** = where)

⚠️ **Common Mistake:** don't say 我有头疼 — say 我头疼 or 我的头很疼.

notes.heading: 🏥 At the Doctor's (看病 kànbìng)
notes.body:
**看病 kànbìng** literally means 'see illness' — to see a doctor.

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 医生 | yīshēng | doctor |
| 医院 | yīyuàn | hospital |
| 看病 | kànbìng | to see a doctor |
| 吃药 | chī yào | to take medicine |
| 怎么了？ | zěnme le? | what's wrong? |

💡 **Worked Example — a mini dialogue:**
Doctor: 你怎么了？Nǐ zěnme le? — What's wrong with you?
Patient: 我头疼，还有点发烧。Wǒ tóuténg, hái yǒudiǎn fāshāo. — I have a headache and a bit of a fever.
Doctor: 你应该多喝水，多休息。Nǐ yīnggāi duō hē shuǐ, duō xiūxi. — You should drink more water and rest more.

📎 **Key Points:**
- 有点儿 **yǒudiǎnr** = a little / a bit: 有点儿不舒服 (a bit unwell).
- 药 **yào** = medicine; remember 吃 is used for taking medicine: 吃药.

notes.heading: 🏃 Healthy Habits (健康 jiànkāng)
notes.body:
健康 **jiànkāng** means 'health / healthy'. Good habits:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 锻炼 | duànliàn | to exercise |
| 运动 | yùndòng | sports / exercise |
| 休息 | xiūxi | to rest |
| 多喝水 | duō hē shuǐ | drink more water |
| 早睡早起 | zǎo shuì zǎo qǐ | early to bed, early to rise |
| 吃水果 | chī shuǐguǒ | eat fruit |

💡 **Worked Example:** 多运动对身体好。Duō yùndòng duì shēntǐ hǎo. — More exercise is good for the body. (对…好 **duì … hǎo** = good for …)

🔑 **How it works:** 多 **duō** (more) + verb is a common advice pattern: 多锻炼 (exercise more), 多休息 (rest more), 多吃水果 (eat more fruit). Its opposite is 少 **shǎo** (less): 少喝可乐 (drink less cola).

📎 **Key Point:** 每天 **měitiān** = every day: 我每天锻炼。I exercise every day.

notes.heading: ✅ Saying 'Should' — 应该
notes.body:
**应该 yīnggāi** means 'should / ought to' and comes before the verb.

**Pattern:** person + 应该 + verb phrase

💡 **Worked Example:**
- 你应该多喝水。Nǐ yīnggāi duō hē shuǐ. — You should drink more water.
- 生病了应该去看医生。Shēngbìng le yīnggāi qù kàn yīshēng. — When you're sick you should go see a doctor.
- 我们不应该吃太多糖。Wǒmen bù yīnggāi chī tài duō táng. — We shouldn't eat too much sugar.

🔑 **How it works:**
- Negative: 不应该 (should not) — 不 goes before 应该.
- Asking for advice: 我应该怎么办？Wǒ yīnggāi zěnme bàn? — What should I do?

📎 **Key Points:**
- 应该 is softer than 必须 **bìxū** (must) — use it for friendly advice.
- Related word: 可以 **kěyǐ** (may / can): 你可以明天来 (you can come tomorrow).

notes.heading: 🔗 Giving Reasons: 因为…所以…
notes.body:
Explain health choices with **因为 yīnwèi … 所以 suǒyǐ …** (because … so …).

💡 **Worked Example:**
- 因为我感冒了，所以我要多休息。Yīnwèi wǒ gǎnmào le, suǒyǐ wǒ yào duō xiūxi. — Because I have a cold, I need to rest more.
- 因为运动对身体好，所以我们应该每天锻炼。Yīnwèi yùndòng duì shēntǐ hǎo, suǒyǐ wǒmen yīnggāi měitiān duànliàn. — Because exercise is good for the body, we should exercise every day.

🔑 **How it works:** unlike English, Chinese can happily use both 'because' AND 'so' in one sentence — 因为 and 所以 often appear together. You may also drop one: 我感冒了，(所以)要休息。

⚠️ **Common Mistake:** translating English word-for-word and leaving out 所以 is fine, but never start a stand-alone sentence with 所以 without a reason first.

✅ **Check:** 'Because I have a stomach ache, I should see a doctor.' → 因为我肚子疼，所以我应该去看医生。

flashcards.example: 我头疼。Wǒ tóu téng. (I have a headache.)
他用右手写字。Tā yòng yòushǒu xiězì. (He writes with his right hand.)

flashcards.definition: Eye(s). Measure word for a pair: 一双眼睛.
flashcards.example: 她的眼睛很大。Tā de yǎnjing hěn dà. (Her eyes are big.)

flashcards.definition: Stomach / tummy. 肚子疼 = stomach ache.
flashcards.example: 我肚子疼，不能去学校。Wǒ dùzi téng, bù néng qù xuéxiào. (My tummy hurts; I can't go to school.)
我感冒了。Wǒ gǎnmào le. (I've caught a cold.)
他发烧了，要去医院。Tā fāshāo le, yào qù yīyuàn. (He has a fever and needs to go to hospital.)
我今天不舒服。Wǒ jīntiān bù shūfu. (I don't feel well today.)

flashcards.definition: To see a doctor — literally 'see illness'.
flashcards.example: 我明天去看病。Wǒ míngtiān qù kànbìng. (I'm going to see a doctor tomorrow.)

flashcards.definition: To take medicine — uses 吃 (eat), not 喝.
flashcards.example: 你应该按时吃药。Nǐ yīnggāi ànshí chī yào. (You should take your medicine on time.)
我每天锻炼半个小时。Wǒ měitiān duànliàn bàn ge xiǎoshí. (I exercise for half an hour every day.)

flashcards.definition: To rest. 多休息 = rest more.
flashcards.example: 你应该多休息。Nǐ yīnggāi duō xiūxi. (You should rest more.)

flashcards.definition: Should / ought to — comes before the verb. Negative: 不应该.
flashcards.example: 我们应该早睡早起。Wǒmen yīnggāi zǎo shuì zǎo qǐ. (We should go to bed early and get up early.)

questions.explanation: 头 tóu means head. 手 is hand, 脚 is foot and 腿 is leg.
感冒 gǎnmào means a cold: 我感冒了 = I've caught a cold. A fever is 发烧.
医生 yīshēng means doctor. A hospital is 医院 and medicine is 药.
应该 yīnggāi means should or ought to — softer than 必须 (must) and used for giving advice.
休息 xiūxi means to rest. Doctors often advise 多休息 (rest more) when you are ill.

questions.stem: 我肚子疼。(Wǒ dùzi téng.) means:
questions.explanation: 肚子 is the tummy and 疼 means hurts — the pattern body part + 疼 expresses pain without needing 'have'.

questions.stem: 看病 (kànbìng) literally means 'see illness' and is used to say:
questions.explanation: 看病 kànbìng is the everyday phrase for consulting a doctor: 我要去看病 (I'm going to see a doctor).

questions.stem: Which verb does Chinese use for 'taking medicine'?
questions.explanation: Medicine is 'eaten' in Chinese: 吃药 chī yào, even if you swallow it with water — never 喝药.

questions.stem: The doctor asks 你怎么了？(Nǐ zěnme le?) What is the best reply?
choices: 我很好，谢谢。Wǒ hěn hǎo, xièxie.
我头疼，还有点发烧。Wǒ tóuténg, hái yǒudiǎn fāshāo.
questions.explanation: 你怎么了？asks what's wrong, so the patient describes symptoms: a headache and a bit of a fever.

questions.stem: 多运动对身体好。(Duō yùndòng duì shēntǐ hǎo.) means:
choices: Too much exercise is bad for the body.
More exercise is good for the body.
questions.explanation: 对…好 means 'good for…', so more exercise is good for the body. The opposite advice would use 少 (less).

questions.stem: How do you say 'You should not eat too much sugar'?
choices: 你不应该吃太多糖。Nǐ bù yīnggāi chī tài duō táng.
你应该不吃太多糖。Nǐ yīnggāi bù chī tài duō táng.
你不可以吃糖很。Nǐ bù kěyǐ chī táng hěn.
你应该多吃糖。Nǐ yīnggāi duō chī táng.
questions.explanation: The negative of 应该 is 不应该 (should not), with 不 before 应该, and 太多 means 'too much': 你不应该吃太多糖.

questions.stem: 因为我感冒了，所以我要多休息。(Yīnwèi wǒ gǎnmào le, suǒyǐ wǒ yào duō xiūxi.) This sentence shows that in Chinese:
choices: 'Because' and 'so' cannot appear in the same sentence
'Because' and 'so' often appear together in one sentence
The reason must always come second
questions.explanation: Unlike English, Chinese commonly pairs 因为 (because) with 所以 (so) in a single sentence — both connectors together are natural.

questions.stem: Which is the natural Chinese way to say 'I have a headache'?
questions.explanation: Pain is expressed as body part + 疼 with no verb 'to have': 我头疼. 我有头疼 and 我是头疼 are common learner errors.

questions.stem: A: 你怎么了？B: 我发烧了。A: 你应该___。Which advice completes the dialogue naturally?
choices: 少喝水 shǎo hē shuǐ — drink less water
多喝水，多休息 duō hē shuǐ, duō xiūxi — drink more water and rest more
多吃糖 duō chī táng — eat more sugar
少睡觉 shǎo shuìjiào — sleep less
questions.explanation: For a fever the sensible advice is more water and more rest; the 多 + verb pattern means 'do more of…' and 少 means 'do less'.

questions.stem: 小红 says: 我最近很不舒服，头疼，还咳嗽。我应该怎么办？(Wǒ zuìjìn hěn bù shūfu, tóuténg, hái késou. Wǒ yīnggāi zěnme bàn?) What is she asking?
choices: What she should do about her symptoms
questions.explanation: 我应该怎么办？means 'what should I do?' — after listing her symptoms (unwell, headache, coughing) she is asking for advice, not for a time or place.
